dish: Kaiseki-style oden served one piece at a time, finished with dashi ramen
w: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka: oden treated like a kaiseki simmered course — tofu under kombu shavings, soft egg with ground sesame — ending in dashi ramen or Edo-style peppered rice.

dish: 'Hakoniwa' miniature seasonal-garden amuse; Nanko plum from the chef's home town of Minabe
w: French restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka themed on aroma ('the nose'); its boxed 'Hakoniwa' amuse and Wakayama Nanko plums are the signatures.

dish: Onion Basque cheesecake; ramen made with house-made pasta
w: Contemporary restaurant added to the MICHELIN Guide by inspectors in July 2026; standouts include a Basque cheesecake made with onion and grilled onigiri.

dish: Osaka Bay white-fish tempura finished with salt-seasoned tendon
w: Added to the MICHELIN Guide in July 2026: white fish from Osaka Bay and the Seto Inland Sea fried in cottonseed oil, ending in the house salt-seasoned tendon.

dish: Sashimi with soy and a dense kombu clear soup
w: Bib Gourmand (2026) izakaya named for the 'immortal jellyfish'; sashimi and a deep kombu clear soup anchor the menu.

dish: Sembajiru (Semba merchants' fish-and-daikon soup) in a chakaiseki course
w: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka: tea-ceremony kaiseki with Osaka touches such as Sembajiru, the old Semba merchant-quarter soup.

dish: Counter tempura course
w: Tempura counter in Nishitemma listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka.

dish: Classic pastry-wrapped (en croûte) fish and meat
w: French restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka where modern starters give way to classic pastry-wrapped fish and meat.

dish: Bisque of Japanese tiger prawn (kuruma-ebi)
w: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka; its Japanese tiger-prawn bisque is the dish inspectors single out.

dish: Rossini Burger (beef with foie gras)
w: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka; the Rossini Burger riffs on the classic beef-and-foie-gras dish.

dish: Basque asado of char-grilled seafood or meat
w: Basque restaurant by Utsubo Park, in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka, known for its char-grilled asado and Spanish wines.

dish: Modern Mexican course built on corn, chilli and cacao imported from Mexico
w: One MICHELIN Star: the first Mexican restaurant in Japan to earn a star, a four-table room in Kita-Horie cooking Indigenous Mexican ingredients and techniques in a modern way.

dish: Cassoulet, quiche Lorraine and beef cheek in red wine
w: French bistro in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka with a menu of country favourites such as cassoulet and beef cheek in red wine.

dish: Drip-drawn dashi soup seasoned only with salt
w: Japanese restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka; the chef draws dashi like drip coffee and serves traditional dishes on modern ceramics.

dish: Awaji lettuce and Agu pork shabu-shabu; roe-laden sweetfish fried in rice paper
w: One MICHELIN Star contemporary restaurant; Agu pork and Awaji lettuce from the chef's parents' farm, served shabu-shabu style, is one of the inspectors' favourite dishes.

dish: Crab gratin, callos (tripe stew) and arroz meloso
w: Spanish restaurant in Fukushima listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka, known for callos and arroz meloso or caldoso.

dish: Duck and foie gras spécialités
w: Counter French run by a husband-and-wife team, listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka; the chef trained under a duck specialist and duck and foie gras are the house dishes.

dish: Raw-prawn ganjang saeu with caviar and kiwi sauce; gimbap presented as rice crackers
w: Korean restaurant added to the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka by inspectors in July 2026, reworking Korean classics such as soy-marinated raw prawn.

dish: Hamburg steak with demi-glace sauce
w: Bib Gourmand (2025) yōshoku house whose lineage goes back to 1935, known for hamburg steak with demi-glace.

dish: Dashi-forward chukasoba ramen with house-made noodles
address: B2F, Semba Center Bldg No. 2, 1-3-2 Sembachuo, Chuo-ku, Osaka 541-0055, Japan
w: Ramen counter under the Semba Center buildings, listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka for a soup built on the brilliance of dashi.

dish: Rice fresh from the kamado stove opening an Italian course
w: Contemporary Italian in Nishitemma, listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka; the meal starts with rice just cooked in a wood-fired kamado.

dish: Unseasoned grilled eel (shirayaki) with stir-fried burdock, after Yawata-maki
w: Japanese restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka with careful ingredient pairings built on dashi, such as shirayaki eel with great burdock.

dish: Counter tempura course
w: Tempura counter on Oimatsu-dōri antiques street, listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka.

dish: French duck and lamb in rich sauces over patiently made consommé
w: Intimate French restaurant on the Uemachi plateau, listed in the MICHELIN Guide Kyoto Osaka for duck and lamb in deep, stock-based sauces.
